title: 15. System Design Case Studies: Design YouTube
summary: Design YouTube at the scale of ~2 B monthly active users and 500 hours of video uploaded every minute: video upload, transcoding to multiple resolutions (HLS adaptive bitrate), CDN-based streaming, search, recommendations, and…
objectives: Step 3: Deep Dive — Data Model (10 min)
Step 4: Deep Dive — Key Algorithms & APIs (10 min)

sections.title: Step 1: Clarify Requirements (5 min)
sections.body:
> **In one line:** Design YouTube at the scale of ~2 B monthly active users and **500 hours of video uploaded every minute**: video upload, transcoding to multiple resolutions (HLS adaptive bitrate), CDN-based streaming, search, recommendations, and engagement tracking. Focus on the **video processing pipeline** (resumable upload → transcoding → HLS packaging → CDN distribution) and the **recommendation system** (two-tower retrieval → deep ranker). ---

### Functional Requirements
- **Upload**: a creator uploads a video (≤ 256 GB, ≤ 12 h), with title, description, tags, thumbnail, and privacy setting (public, unlisted, private).
- **Transcode**: the system generates multiple resolutions (240p, 360p, 480p, 720p, 1080p, 1440p, 4K, 8K) and codecs (H.264, VP9, AV1) plus HLS/DASH segments for adaptive streaming.
- **Watch**: a viewer plays the video; the player picks the highest sustainable bitrate and adapts on the fly.
- **Search**: by title, channel, tag, content (semantic search optional).
- **Recommendations**: a personalized "Up Next" feed on the home page and after each video.
- **Like / comment / subscribe**: counts + lists; notifications to the channel.
- **Live streaming**: real-time broadcast (separate pipeline — covered briefly).
- **Shorts**: ≤ 60 s vertical videos with algorithmic feed (like Reels).
- **Engagement telemetry**: watch time, retention curve, click-through — for ranking and creator analytics.

### Non-Functional Requirements
- **Availability** 99.99% for streaming (≈ 52 min downtime/year) — outage is front-page news.
- **Latency**: time-to-first-frame p99 < 1.5 s; seek latency p99 < 500 ms.
- **Scale**: 2 B MAU, 1 B hours watched/day, 500 hours uploaded/min, ~5 B video views/day.
- **Throughput**: video uploads ~1 PB/day (500 h/min × avg 50 MB/min after compression); video egress ~50 PB/day.
- **Storage**: 1 PB/day uploads → 365 PB/year raw + transcoded replicas (5–10× raw) → ~3–5 EB/year total.
- **Durability** 11 nines for video (object storage with multi-region replication).
- **Adaptive streaming**: player must switch bitrates within 2 s of bandwidth change.
- **Consistency**: eventual consistency OK for view counts (≤ 5 min lag); strong for "did I upload it?" (creator sees own video immediately).

### Back-of-Envelope Estimation
- **Upload bandwidth**: 500 h/min × 60 min/h × 5 MB/min (avg raw) = 150 GB/min = 2.5 GB/s sustained.
- **Transcoding cost**: each video transcoded to ~6 resolutions × 2 codecs = 12 variants. CPU cost ≈ 0.5–2× realtime per variant. 500 h/min × 12 variants × 1× = 6 000 h of CPU per minute of wall clock → 360 servers each running 1× realtime, or ~6 000 CPU cores at 100% utilization.
- **Storage**: 1 PB/day raw × 10× (transcoded replicas + thumbnails + HLS segments) = 10 PB/day. Lifecycle: hot → warm (90 days) → cold (Glacier) at 1 year.
- **Egress**: 5 B views/day × avg 30 MB/view (partial watch) = 150 PB/day. CDN absorbs 95%+ → ~7.5 PB/day origin.
- **Recommendations**: each user session triggers ~10 recommendation requests. 2 B MAU × 10 = 20 B rec requests/day = ~230 k QPS avg.

### Scope
- **In scope**: upload pipeline, transcoding, HLS packaging, CDN distribution, recommendations (high level), engagement tracking, scaling.
- **Out of scope**: ML model internals, ads/monetization, content moderation (separate pipeline), live streaming details (separate design), DRM (mention but don't deep-dive).

sections.title: Step 2: High-Level Architecture (10 min)
sections.body:
### Components 1. **Global DNS + Anycast** (Google's edge DNS) — routes viewer to nearest CDN POP. 2. **CDN / Edge POP** (Google's GGC — Google Global Cache, plus Akamai tier-2) — caches HLS segments at 200+ POPs worldwide. 95%+ cache hit ratio for popular videos. 3. **API Gateway / Frontend** — TLS, OAuth, rate limiting, request routing. Powered by Go / C++ at YouTube scale. 4. **Upload service** — handles resumable uploads, returns presigned URLs to the client; the client uploads bytes directly to object storage (bypassing the API server for bandwidth efficiency). 5. **Object storage** (Google Cloud Storage / S3) — raw uploads bucket + processed bucket. 11-nines durability, multi-region replication. 6. **Transcoding pipeline**: - **Ingest worker** — pulls raw video from object storage, probes it (FFprobe) for duration, codec, resolution. - **Transcoder farm** — FFmpeg with hardware acceleration (Intel QSV, NVIDIA NVENC). Generates multiple resolutions + codecs in parallel. - **Packager** — segments video into HLS (.m3u8 + .ts) or DASH (.mpd + .m4s) chunks; encrypts with AES-128 if DRM required. - **Thumbnail generator** — extracts keyframes at multiple timestamps; ML picks the best thumbnail. 7. **Metadata store** — Spanner / Postgres-sharded for video metadata (title, description, tags, channel, view count). 8. **Search index** — Elasticsearch / Google's in-house (the famous "Megastore + reverse index" → now Colossus + search). Inverted index on title/description/tags. 9. **Recommendation system**: - **Candidate generator** — two-tower ANN over video embeddings (FAISS / ScaNN). - **Ranker** — deep NN predicting watch time, engagement, satisfaction. 10. **Engagement tracking** — Kafka stream of play events (every 10 s) → Flink aggregation → Spanner/Cassandra for analytics. 11. **Notification service** — pushes new-video alerts to subscribers via APNS/FCM/web push. 12. **CDN origin shield** — a regional cache tier that protects object storage from thundering-herd when a new viral video drops. ### Mermaid Diagram ```mermaid flowchart LR C([Creator]) -->|presigned URL| UP[Upload service] UP --> S3U[(GCS / S3
raw uploads)] C -->|POST metadata| API[API Gateway] API --> MD[Metadata svc
Spanner] API --> K1[(Kafka: video-uploaded)] K1 --> ING[Ingest worker
FFprobe] ING --> TR[Transcoder farm
FFmpeg + NVENC] TR --> PKG[HLS / DASH packager] TR --> TH[Thumbnailer
ML pick] PKG --> S3P[(GCS processed
HLS segments)] TH --> S3P S3P --> CDN[Google Global Cache
+ Akamai CDN] V([Viewer]) --> DNS[Edge DNS] DNS --> CDN CDN -->|HLS hit| V V -->|engagement| K2[(Kafka: play-events)] K2 --> FL[Flink aggregation] FL --> AN[(Cassandra
analytics)] API --> REC[Recommender
two-tower + ranker] REC --> EMB[(FAISS
video embeddings)] API --> SRCH[Search service
Elasticsearch] API --> NOTIF[Notification svc] NOTIF --> PUSH[APNS / FCM] ``` ### ASCII Diagram ``` +---------------------+ | Creator (browser) | +---+-------------+---+ | | presigned | | POST /videos URL | | (metadata) v v +-----+---+ +----+--------+ | GCS raw | | API Gateway | | uploads | +----+--------+ +----+----+ | | +---> Spanner (metadata) | +---> Kafka: video-uploaded | | v v +----+----+ +--------+--------+ |Ingest | | Recommender | |worker | | (ANN + ranker) | |(FFprobe)| +--------+--------+ +----+----+ | | v v FAISS embeddings +----+----+ |Transcoder farm +----------+ |(FFmpeg + NVENC) | Search | | 6 resolutions × 2 codec| (ES) | +----+--------+ +----------+ | | v v +----+----+ +-----+------+ |HLS/DASH | |Thumbnailer | |packager | |(ML pick) | +----+----+ +-----+------+ | | +-----+------+ | v +------+------+ +--------+ | GCS processed| | Flink |<--- Kafka play-events | HLS segments | | (watch | +------+------+ | time) | | +---+----+ v | +----------+----------+ v | Google Global Cache | Cassandra | (CDN edge, 95% hit) | (analytics) +---------+-----------+ | v +-------+------+ | Viewer app | +--------------+ ``` ### Request Flow Walkthrough 1. **Upload**: Creator selects a file → app calls `POST /api/v1/videos/upload/start` → upload service returns a presigned GCS URL + `video_id` → app uploads bytes **directly to GCS** (resumable, parallel chunks) → app calls `POST /api/v1/videos/{id}` with metadata (title, description, tags, privacy) → metadata service writes to Spanner, publishes `video-uploaded` event to Kafka, returns `202 Accepted {status: processing}`. 2. **Transcoding**: Kafka consumer (ingest worker) reads `video-uploaded`, pulls raw video from GCS, probes it (FFprobe), and dispatches transcoding jobs to the transcoder farm. Each transcoder produces one (resolution, codec) variant using FFmpeg with hardware acceleration. Outputs: 6 resolutions × 2 codecs = 12 variants. Packager segments each variant into 10-s HLS chunks. Thumbnailer extracts 5 candidate frames; ML picks the best. 3. **Publish**: All variants + thumbnails + HLS playlists written to `processed/` GCS bucket. CDN cache pre-warmed for likely-popular videos (creator with > 10 k subscribers). `video-ready` event published. Video becomes searchable; subscribers notified. 4. **Watch**: Viewer `GET /api/v1/videos/{id}/stream` → API returns the `master.m3u8` playlist URL → player fetches the playlist (lists available bitrates) → picks the highest sustainable bitrate → fetches `.ts` segments from CDN edge. Player adapts every 2 s based on measured bandwidth. Engagement events (play, pause, seek, every 10 s of watch time) sent to Kafka. 5. **Search**: `GET /api/v1/search?q=cats` → search service queries Elasticsearch (or Google's reverse index) → returns ranked video list. 6. **Recommendations**: Home page → `GET /api/v1/recommendations` → recommender retrieves user embedding from Redis → ANN over video embeddings (FAISS) → top 1 000 candidates → deep ranker → top 20 returned.

sections.title: Step 3: Deep Dive — Data Model (10 min)
sections.body:
### Tables / Schema

**Spanner — `videos` (video metadata, globally consistent)**
```sql
CREATE TABLE videos (
    video_id         STRING(16) PRIMARY KEY,
    channel_id       STRING(16) NOT NULL,
    title            STRING(100),
    description      STRING(5000),
    tags             ARRAY<STRING>,
    duration_seconds INT64,
    privacy          STRING(10),         -- public | unlisted | private
    status           STRING(20),         -- processing | ready | failed | deleted
    uploaded_at      TIMESTAMP,
    published_at     TIMESTAMP,
    view_count       INT64,
    like_count       INT64,
    dislike_count    INT64,
    comment_count    INT64,
    thumbnail_url    STRING(255)
) INTERLEAVE IN PARENT channels ON DELETE CASCADE;
```

**Spanner — `channels`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE channels (
    channel_id     STRING(16) PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id        STRING(16),
    name           STRING(100),
    subscriber_count INT64,
    total_views    INT64,
    created_at     TIMESTAMP
);
```

**Cassandra — `video_variants` (transcoded variants, write-heavy)**
```sql
CREATE TABLE video_variants (
    video_id     UUID,
    resolution   TEXT,           -- 240p | 360p | 480p | 720p | 1080p | 1440p | 4K | 8K
    codec        TEXT,           -- h264 | vp9 | av1
    bitrate      INT,
    hls_url      TEXT,           -- master.m3u8 for this variant
    size_bytes   BIGINT,
    PRIMARY KEY (video_id, resolution, codec)
);
```

**Cassandra — `engagement_events` (per-user watch telemetry)**
```sql
CREATE TABLE engagement_events (
    user_id      BIGINT,
    video_id     BIGINT,
    event_type   TEXT,            -- play | pause | seek | watch_10s | complete
    position_s   INT,             -- playback position when event fired
    ts           TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, video_id, ts)
) WITH CLUSTERING ORDER BY (video_id ASC, ts DESC);
```

**Postgres — `comments` (relational, supports threading)**
```sql
CREATE TABLE comments (
    comment_id   BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    video_id     BIGINT,
    parent_id    BIGINT,           -- NULL for top-level
    user_id      BIGINT,
    text         TEXT,
    like_count   INT,
    created_at   TIMESTAMP
);
CREATE INDEX idx_comments_video ON comments(video_id, created_at DESC);
```

**Redis — `video_emb:{video_id}` (vector embedding for recommendations)**
```
SET video_emb:{video_id}  [0.12, -0.45, 0.78, ...]   // 256-dim float32 vector
```

**Redis — `rec_cache:{user_id}` (precomputed recommendation cache, 5-min TTL)**
```
LPUSH rec_cache:{user_id}  {video_id}:{score}:{ts}
```

### Indexes
- Spanner: PRIMARY KEY on `video_id`; secondary interleaved on `channels` for fast channel-page scans.
- Cassandra `video_variants`: PRIMARY KEY `(video_id, resolution, codec)` — all variants for a video are co-located.
- Cassandra `engagement_events`: PRIMARY KEY `(user_id, video_id, ts)` — supports "what did this user watch?" and "watch history for this video."
- Postgres `comments`: index on `(video_id, created_at)` for fast comment fetching.
- Elasticsearch: inverted index on `title`, `description`, `tags`. Vector index for semantic search.
- FAISS: ANN index on video embeddings (256-dim, IVF with PQ for memory efficiency).

### Storage Choice
- **Spanner** for video/channel metadata — globally consistent, horizontally scalable, SQL semantics. YouTube's metadata is too critical for eventual consistency.
- **Cassandra** for engagement events and variants — write-heavy, time-series, no joins.
- **GCS / S3** for video files and HLS segments — 11-nines durability, lifecycle to Glacier at 1 year.
- **Redis** for recommendation caches and embeddings — sub-ms vector ops via FAISS in-process.
- **Postgres** for comments — relational, supports threading, manageable size (1 video = avg 100 comments).
- **Elasticsearch** for search — inverted index, fast fuzzy matching, supports ranking signals.

sections.title: Step 4: Deep Dive — Key Algorithms & APIs (10 min)
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Upload large video files in parallel chunks with resume capability.
- Transcode one (resolution, codec) variant using FFmpeg + NVENC.
- Segment an MP4 into HLS (.m3u8 + .ts) chunks for adaptive streaming.
- Top-level: transcode all variants in parallel, then build master playlist.
- Start a resumable upload
- Finalize upload + publish metadata
- Get video metadata + stream URL
- Get adaptive bitrate playlist

**Defines:** `resumable_upload()`, `transcode_variant()`, `package_hls()`, `transcode_video()`, `get_recommendations()`

### API Design
```
# Start a resumable upload
POST   /api/v1/videos/upload/start
       { filename, size, content_type }
       -> 200 OK { video_id, upload_url (presigned GCS), expires_in: 3600 }

# Finalize upload + publish metadata
POST   /api/v1/videos/{video_id}
       { title, description, tags, privacy, thumbnail_ts }
       -> 202 Accepted { status: processing }

# Get video metadata + stream URL
GET    /api/v1/videos/{video_id}
       -> 200 OK { title, channel, hls_master_url, ... }

# Get adaptive bitrate playlist
GET    /api/v1/videos/{video_id}/stream
       -> 200 OK { master_m3u8_url, expires_in: 3600 }

# Search
GET    /api/v1/search?q=cats&filter=short
       -> 200 OK { videos: [...] }

# Recommendations (home page)
GET    /api/v1/recommendations?cursor=...
       -> 200 OK { videos: [...], next_cursor }

# Engagement event (from player)
POST   /api/v1/videos/{video_id}/events
       { type: watch_10s, position_s: 60 }

# Like / comment / subscribe
POST   /api/v1/videos/{id}/likes
POST   /api/v1/videos/{id}/comments
POST   /api/v1/channels/{id}/subscriptions
```

### Key Algorithms

#### (1) Resumable upload with parallel chunked PUT

```python
import os, requests, hashlib

CHUNK_SIZE = 8 * 1024 * 1024   # 8 MB chunks (Google resumable upload standard)

def resumable_upload(file_path: str, content_type: str, video_id: str, upload_url: str):
    """Upload large video files in parallel chunks with resume capability."""
    file_size = os.path.getsize(file_path)
    chunks = [(start, min(CHUNK_SIZE, file_size - start))
              for start in range(0, file_size, CHUNK_SIZE)]

    def upload_chunk(args):
        start, length = args
        end = start + length - 1
        headers = {
            "Content-Range": f"bytes {start}-{end}/{file_size}",
            "Content-Type": content_type,
        }
        with open(file_path, "rb") as f:
            f.seek(start)
            data = f.read(length)
        # Retry with exponential backoff on transient failures
        for attempt in range(5):
            r = requests.put(upload_url, headers=headers, data=data)
            if r.status_code in (200, 201, 308):
                return True
            time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
        return False

    # Parallel chunked upload
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool:
        results = list(pool.map(upload_chunk, chunks))

    if not all(results):
        # Resume: query GCS for which chunks are already uploaded
        r = requests.head(upload_url, headers={"Content-Range": f"bytes */{file_size}"})
        # GCS returns 308 with Range header indicating uploaded bytes
        # Retry missing chunks only
        raise UploadIncomplete("resume from " + r.headers.get("Range", ""))
    return True
```

#### (2) Transcoding pipeline — parallel variants with hardware acceleration

```python
import subprocess

RESOLUTIONS = [
    # (label, height, bitrate_kbps)
    ("240p",  240,  400),
    ("360p",  360,  800),
    ("480p",  480, 1200),
    ("720p",  720, 2500),
    ("1080p", 1080, 5000),
    ("1440p", 1440, 9000),
    ("4K",    2160, 17000),
]
CODECS = ["h264", "vp9", "av1"]   # AV1 for new content; H.264 for compatibility

def transcode_variant(input_path: str, output_dir: str,
                      resolution: str, height: int, bitrate: int, codec: str):
    """Transcode one (resolution, codec) variant using FFmpeg + NVENC."""
    output_path = f"{output_dir}/{resolution}_{codec}.mp4"
    # Use hardware-accelerated encoder (NVENC for h264, NVENC VP9 or CPU for av1)
    if codec == "h264":
        enc = "h264_nvenc -preset p4 -tune ll"
    elif codec == "vp9":
        enc = "libvpx-vp9 -row-mt 1 -b:v {bitrate}k"
    else:  # av1
        enc = "libsvtav1 -preset 6"

    cmd = (
        f"ffmpeg -i {input_path} "
        f"-vf scale=-2:{height} "                   # keep aspect ratio
        f"-c:v {enc} -b:v {bitrate}k "
        f"-c:a aac -b:a 128k "
        f"-movflags +faststart {output_path}"
    )
    subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, check=True)
    return output_path

def package_hls(variant_path: str, output_dir: str):
    """Segment an MP4 into HLS (.m3u8 + .ts) chunks for adaptive streaming."""
    cmd = (
        f"ffmpeg -i {variant_path} "
        f"-c copy -f hls -hls_time 10 "             # 10-second segments
        f"-hls_playlist_type vod "
        f"-hls_segment_filename '{output_dir}/seg_%05d.ts' "
        f"{output_dir}/playlist.m3u8"
    )
    subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, check=True)

def transcode_video(video_id: str, raw_path: str):
    """Top-level: transcode all variants in parallel, then build master playlist."""
    output_dir = f"gs://yt-processed/{video_id}/"
    # Parallel variant transcoding (each on a separate worker)
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(RESOLUTIONS) * len(CODECS)) as pool:
        futures = []
        for resolution, height, bitrate in RESOLUTIONS:
            for codec in CODECS:
                futures.append(pool.submit(transcode_variant,
                                           raw_path, output_dir,
                                           resolution, height, bitrate, codec))
        for f in futures:
            f.result()   # propagate exceptions

    # Package each variant into HLS segments
    for resolution, _, _ in RESOLUTIONS:
        for codec in CODECS:
            variant_path = f"{output_dir}/{resolution}_{codec}.mp4"
            package_hls(variant_path, f"{output_dir}/{resolution}_{codec}/")

    # Build master.m3u8 playlist listing all variants
    build_master_playlist(video_id, RESOLUTIONS, CODECS)

    # Generate thumbnail candidates and pick best with ML
    generate_thumbnails(raw_path, video_id)

    # Mark video as ready
    publish_video_ready(video_id)
```

#### (3) Recommendation candidate retrieval (two-tower ANN)

```python
import faiss
import numpy as np

# Pre-built FAISS index of all video embeddings (256-dim, IVF + PQ for memory)
VIDEO_INDEX = faiss.read_index("gs://yt-rec/video_index.faiss")   # ~100M videos, ~25 GB

def get_recommendations(user_id: int, top_k: int = 20, candidate_pool: int = 1000):
    # 1. Fetch user embedding (updated by a streaming job from watch history)
    user_emb = redis.get(f"user_emb:{user_id}")   # 256-dim float32
    user_emb = np.frombuffer(user_emb, dtype=np.float32).reshape(1, -1)

    # 2. ANN retrieval — top candidate_pool videos by cosine similarity
    distances, video_ids = VIDEO_INDEX.search(user_emb, candidate_pool)
    candidates = video_ids[0].tolist()

    # 3. Filter: exclude already-watched, age-restricted, region-blocked
    watched = redis.smembers(f"watched:{user_id}")
    candidates = [v for v in candidates if str(v) not in watched]
    candidates = filter_by_region(candidates, user_id)
    candidates = filter_by_age(candidates, user_id)

    # 4. Fetch candidate metadata (batch)
    metadata = batch_get_video_metadata(candidates)

    # 5. Deep ranker: predict watch time, satisfaction, engagement
    ranked = deep_ranker(user_id, candidates, metadata, top_k=top_k)

    # 6. Diversity: ensure no more than 3 from same channel
    ranked = diversify(ranked, max_per_channel=3)

    return ranked[:top_k]
```

sections.title: Step 5: Scalability & Reliability (5 min)
sections.body:
### Scaling Challenges
- **500 hours uploaded/min**: transcoding is CPU-bound. Solution: a transcoder farm of thousands of workers (auto-scaled), each with hardware acceleration (NVENC). Job queue (Kafka) absorbs spikes.
- **5 B views/day = ~50 PB/day egress**: only CDN edge can serve this. Solution: Google Global Cache (GGC) at 200+ POPs; 95%+ hit ratio for popular videos.
- **Viral video thundering herd**: a new viral video drops → millions of viewers hit the same segments. Solution: origin shield (regional cache tier) protects object storage; pre-warm CDN for likely-viral videos.
- **Recommendations at 230 k QPS**: ANN over 100 M videos is expensive. Solution: IVF + PQ FAISS index (25 GB, sub-ms search); per-user result cache (5-min TTL).
- **Engagement event firehose**: 5 B views × 30 events/view = 150 B events/day. Solution: Kafka → Flink aggregation → rollup to per-video per-hour stats in Cassandra.
- **Storage growth**: 1 PB/day raw × 10× transcoded = 10 PB/day. Solution: lifecycle to Glacier at 1 year; delete orphaned variants; deduplicate identical segments across resolutions.

### Caching Strategy
- **L1 — CDN edge (GGC)**: HLS segments, thumbnails. TTL 24 h; 95%+ hit ratio.
- **L2 — Origin shield**: regional cache tier in front of GCS. TTL 1 h; protects GCS from thundering herds.
- **L3 — Redis metadata cache**: video metadata (title, channel, view count). TTL 60 s; invalidated on update.
- **L4 — Redis recommendation cache**: per-user recommendation list. TTL 5 min.
- **L5 — Redis user-embedding cache**: per-user vector. TTL 1 h; updated by streaming job.
- **L6 — FAISS in-process**: video embedding index, loaded into worker memory at startup (25 GB, shared across requests on the same worker pool).

### Failure Modes
| Failure | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Transcoder farm overloaded | Uploads pile up, creators wait hours | Auto-scale based on queue depth; cap parallel jobs per video; degrade to fewer variants if queue > 1 h |
| CDN edge node down | Viewers in that region get slow streams | DNS health check removes node; traffic rerouted to nearest healthy POP |
| GCS bucket region outage | New uploads fail in that region | Multi-region buckets; upload service fails over to alternate region |
| FAISS index corrupted | Recommendations break | Restore from nightly backup; fall back to popularity-based recs ("Trending") |
| Kafka broker down | Engagement events dropped | Multi-broker RF=3; consumers commit offset only after Cassandra write |
| Spanner split-brain | Metadata writes inconsistent | Spanner's Paxos consensus prevents split-brain by design |
| Viral video segment 0 cache miss | 1 M viewers hit origin simultaneously | Origin shield absorbs; pre-warm top-10 segments for likely-viral videos |
| Player bandwidth drop | Stream stutters | Adaptive bitrate player drops to lower resolution within 2 s |

diagram.title: Step 5: Scalability & Reliability (5 min) — step by step

steps.label: Scaling Challenges
steps.narration: 500 hours uploaded/min: transcoding is CPU-bound. Solution: a transcoder farm of thousands of workers (auto-scaled), each with hardware acceleration (NVENC).

steps.label: Caching Strategy
steps.narration: L1 — CDN edge (GGC): HLS segments, thumbnails. TTL 24 h; 95%+ hit ratio.

quiz.question: Why does YouTube transcode every video into 12+ variants instead of just serving the original?
options: Watch-time tracking is critical — it drives recommendations, creator payouts, and analytics.
Three likely causes. (1) Bot filtering lag: YouTube's bot detection runs continuously but final counts are reconciled nightly.
Content ID is YouTube's copyright system. (1) Reference library: copyright holders upload reference files (their songs, movies) to YouTube.
Three reasons. (1) Adaptive bitrate streaming: viewers have wildly different bandwidth (rural DSL at 1 Mbps, fiber at 1 Gbps, mobile at 5 Mbps).
quiz.explanation: Three reasons. (1) Adaptive bitrate streaming: viewers have wildly different bandwidth (rural DSL at 1 Mbps, fiber at 1 Gbps, mobile at 5 Mbps). If we served only the original 4K upload, mobile users would buffer constantly.

quiz.question: How does HLS adaptive bitrate streaming actually work?
options: Several optimizations. (1) Chunked transcoding: instead of transcoding the whole video sequentially, split it into 10-min chunks and transcode each chunk in parallel on different workers.
Watch-time tracking is critical — it drives recommendations, creator payouts, and analytics.
Content ID is YouTube's copyright system. (1) Reference library: copyright holders upload reference files (their songs, movies) to YouTube.
HLS (HTTP Live Streaming, Apple's protocol) works as follows.
quiz.explanation: HLS (HTTP Live Streaming, Apple's protocol) works as follows. (1) The server segments each video variant into small chunks (10 s each) and stores them as .ts files with a .m3u8 playlist per variant. (2) The server also publishes a master.m3u8 playlist that lists all variants with their bitrates and resolutions.

quiz.question: How does YouTube's recommendation system work at a high level?
options: Watch-time tracking is critical — it drives recommendations, creator payouts, and analytics.
4K live is significantly harder than 1080p live. (1) Encoder cost: 4K encoding is ~4× the CPU of 1080p.
Several optimizations. (1) Chunked transcoding: instead of transcoding the whole video sequentially, split it into 10-min chunks and transcode each chunk in parallel on different workers.
YouTube's recommender is a two-stage retrieval + ranking pipeline.
quiz.explanation: YouTube's recommender is a two-stage retrieval + ranking pipeline. Stage 1 — Candidate generation: instead of scanning all 100 M+ videos, we use approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) over video embeddings. Each video is embedded into a 256-dim vector by a neural network trained on co-watch signals (users who watched A also watched B) and content features (title, tags, thumbnail).

quiz.question: How does YouTube handle a new viral video that gets 100 M views in 24 hours?
options: Resumable, parallel, chunked uploads. (1) Presigned URL: the client calls POST /upload/start to get a presigned GCS URL and a video_id.
Live streaming is fundamentally different from VOD. (1) Ingest: streamer's app pushes RTMP/SRT to a regional ingest endpoint.
Multi-pronged. (1) AV1 for popular videos: re-transcode the top 10 k most-watched videos to AV1 (30–50% smaller than H.264).
Five defenses. (1) CDN edge caching: as soon as a segment is requested from a POP, it's cached for 24 h.
quiz.explanation: Five defenses. (1) CDN edge caching: as soon as a segment is requested from a POP, it's cached for 24 h. With 100 M views across 200 POPs, each POP serves ~500 k views — all cache hits after the first request per segment.

quiz.question: How does YouTube handle the upload of a 100 GB video without timing out?
options: Live streaming is fundamentally different from VOD. (1) Ingest: streamer's app pushes RTMP/SRT to a regional ingest endpoint.
Five defenses. (1) CDN edge caching: as soon as a segment is requested from a POP, it's cached for 24 h.
Multi-pronged. (1) AV1 for popular videos: re-transcode the top 10 k most-watched videos to AV1 (30–50% smaller than H.264).
Resumable, parallel, chunked uploads. (1) Presigned URL: the client calls POST /upload/start to get a presigned GCS URL and a video_id.
quiz.explanation: Resumable, parallel, chunked uploads. (1) Presigned URL: the client calls POST /upload/start to get a presigned GCS URL and a video_id. The URL allows the client to upload bytes directly to GCS, bypassing our API servers — this avoids saturating our bandwidth and lets GCS handle the heavy lifting.
